title: Awesome Tech Talks video record
description: One record per talk. Every file in DATA/videos/ validates against this schema, and DATA/manifest.jsonl holds the same records one per line for bulk export into an AI tool.

id.description: Stable slug for the talk, shaped as speaker-or-topic-hint-year. Also the filename in DATA/videos/ and INFO/{channel}/.

title.description: Title of the talk as published on YouTube.

channel.description: YouTube channel that published the talk.

speakers.description: Everyone speaking on camera, hosts included. Uses ["unknown"] when the source gives no attribution and the transcript does not identify anyone.

date.description: Publication date in ISO form, or the literal string unknown when the source did not carry one. Dates are never inferred.

format.description: Delivery format, judged from the content and tone of the transcript.

level.description: Assumed background needed to follow the talk.

topics.description: One to three topics from a fixed list. The list is closed so that filtering stays predictable across the whole dataset.

description.description: The publisher's own description, carried over verbatim.

entities.description: Every named product, feature, model, codename, standard, or tool mentioned, including terms that appear only once. This field feeds glossary and jargon lookups.

heading.description: What this stretch of the talk is actually about, specific enough that reading the headings alone gives you the structure of the talk.

text.description: The transcript for this segment with verbal filler, false starts, and immediate restatement removed. Named things, numbers, claims, reasoning chains, and anecdotes are preserved in full.

segments.description: The talk broken at real topic shifts. Concatenating every text field gives you the full cleaned talk in order.

read_time_minutes.description: Estimated reading time for the cleaned segment text at 250 words per minute.
